name: Agave Landscape and Ancient Industrial Facilities of Tequila
description: Rows of blue agave stretch across the highlands of Jalisco, Mexico, between the Tequila Volcano and the deep valley of the Rio Grande. This working landscape covers about 34,658 hectares and includes the towns of Tequila, Arenal and Amatitan, where distilleries still turn roasted agave hearts into tequila. Long before the spirit existed, the Teuchitlan people shaped these slopes with terraces, temples and ball courts.
